newsitem.title: JAPAN: CBOT, LIFFE officials seek Japanese investment.
newsitem.headline: CBOT, LIFFE officials seek Japanese investment.

text.p: A planned link between the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) and the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) will provide more opportunities for Japanese investors, officials from the exchanges said on Tuesday.
"There is an awful lot of interest (in the linkage) from institutional investors," said James Borowicz, senior managing director for CBOT's education and marketing services.
Once the linkage starts on May 9, U.S. Treasury bond (T-bond) futures and options will be traded on LIFFE, and German Bund futures and options will be traded on CBOT.
The linkage with CBOT will remain in effect even after European economic and monetary union (EMU) takes place in 1999, said Nicholas Carew Hunt, market secretary of LIFFE.
"(After the EMU) when LIFFE lists a euro (-denominated) bond contract, that will be subject to the link, and CBOT will still have access to a benchmark European bond futures contract," Hunt said.
The link will give LIFFE access to open interest on CBOT, and CBOT access to open interest on LIFFE, allowing traders to adjust their positions on LIFFE by trading on CBOT and vice versa, Hunt added.
The link will also provide more opportunities for Japanese investors to trade by lengthening trading hours for T-bond futures and bund futures, said CBOT's Borowicz.
"(Japanese) customers holding deutschemark portfolios can use the Bund to hedge their portfolios. They didn't have this in their own time zones before," Borowicz said.
The officials made the remarks at a news conference in Tokyo, which they are visiting to promote the exchanges.
Once the linkage starts, Japanese traders will be able to trade Bund futures during Tokyo morning hours by trading in CBOT's night session.
They will also be able to start trading in T-bond futures in Tokyo afternoon, without having to wait for CBOT's day session to begin, by trading during LIFFE's pit session.
